# Hotjar vs OpenReplay (2026)

## Overview
Hotjar and OpenReplay are two popular tools used for session recording, heatmaps, and user feedback. These tools benefit product managers, UX designers, and marketers who want to understand user behavior and improve their website's user experience. The core use case for both tools is to provide insights into how users interact with a website, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Hotjar offers a free plan with limited features, while OpenReplay is free and self-hosted, with no costs per user.
* Data ownership: OpenReplay allows users to own their data, while Hotjar stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Hotjar is generally easier to set up, with a simpler installation process, while OpenReplay requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: OpenReplay is designed to handle large volumes of traffic and can be scaled horizontally, while Hotjar has limitations on its free plan.
* Feature difference: OpenReplay offers more advanced filtering and segmentation options, while Hotjar has a more user-friendly interface.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Hotjar | OpenReplay |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $32-$80+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $39.60-$79.20/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $158.40-$316.80/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Hotjar:**
* Easy to set up and use
* User-friendly interface
* Offers a free plan with limited features
* Integrates with popular tools like Google Analytics
* Limited control over data and scalability
**OpenReplay:**
* Free and self-hosted, with no costs per user
* Allows users to own their data
* Designed to handle large volumes of traffic
* Offers advanced filtering and segmentation options
* Requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain

## When to Choose Each
Hotjar is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams who want a user-friendly interface and don't need advanced features. It's also a good option for teams who don't have the technical expertise to set up and maintain a self-hosted solution. OpenReplay, on the other hand, is a good choice for larger teams who need more control over their data and want to reduce costs. It's also a good option for teams who have the technical expertise to set up and maintain a self-hosted solution and need advanced features like filtering and segmentation.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Hotjar in JSON format.
2. Set up an OpenReplay instance on your server.
3. Use the OpenReplay import tool to import your data from the JSON file.
4. Configure your OpenReplay instance to match your Hotjar setup.
5. Test your OpenReplay instance to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
OpenReplay is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that OpenReplay requires a significant amount of server resources to handle large volumes of traffic. However, for teams who need more control over their data and want to reduce costs, OpenReplay is a good choice, and we recommend switching from Hotjar to OpenReplay if you have the technical expertise and need advanced features.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams with less than 10 users who don't need advanced features and want to reduce costs
* Medium-sized teams with 10-50 users who need more control over their data and want to scale their solution
* Large teams with more than 50 users who need advanced features like filtering and segmentation
* Teams who prioritize data ownership and want to self-host their solution
* Teams who have the technical expertise to set up and maintain a self-hosted solution and want to reduce costs

## FAQ

The main difference between Hotjar and OpenReplay is that OpenReplay is free and self-hosted, while Hotjar offers a free plan with limited features and charges per user.
### Can I export my data from Hotjar and import it into OpenReplay?
Yes, you can export your data from Hotjar in JSON format and import it into OpenReplay using the OpenReplay import tool.
### Is OpenReplay production-ready for most users?
No, OpenReplay is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain.

# Canva vs Penpot (2026)

## Overview
Canva and Penpot are two popular design and collaboration tools used for creating visual content, such as graphics, presentations, and websites. This comparison is beneficial for individuals, teams, and businesses looking to switch from a proprietary platform to a self-hosted, open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is graphic design and collaboration, and someone would switch to take advantage of Penpot's self-hosting capabilities and open-source nature.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Canva offers a free plan and paid plans starting at $15/user/month, while Penpot is free and open-source.
* Data ownership: Penpot allows users to self-host and have full control over their data, whereas Canva stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Canva has a more straightforward setup process, while Penpot requires more technical expertise for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Penpot is more scalable due to its self-hosting capabilities and open-source nature.
* Integration: Canva has a more extensive library of integrations with third-party apps, while Penpot has a growing list of integrations, including support for Figma files.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Canva | Penpot |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $15-$30/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $15/user/month (approx. $750/month) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $15/user/month (approx. $3,000/month) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Canva:**
* User-friendly interface
* Extensive library of templates and design assets
* Collaborative features
* Integrations with third-party apps
* Limited control over data storage and security
**Penpot:**
* Self-hosting capabilities
* Open-source and free
* Customizable and scalable
* Growing community and support
* Limited integrations with third-party apps
* Steeper learning curve due to self-hosting requirements

## When to Choose Each
Canva is suitable for small to medium-sized teams, individuals, or businesses that require a user-friendly interface and a wide range of integrations with third-party apps. It is ideal for those who prioritize ease of use and are willing to compromise on data ownership and control. On the other hand, Penpot is perfect for larger teams, enterprises, or organizations that require self-hosting capabilities, open-source software, and customization options. It is ideal for those who prioritize data ownership, security, and scalability.

## Migration Path
1. Export your designs from Canva in PNG, JPEG, or SVG format.
2. Use the Penpot import tool to upload your designs to Penpot.
3. Set up your Penpot self-hosted server and configure the necessary settings.
4. Invite your team members to collaborate on your designs in Penpot.
5. Explore Penpot's features and customization options to optimize your workflow.

## Our Take
Penpot is still in the process of maturing as a production-ready platform, and some users may encounter bugs or limitations. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Penpot's support for certain file formats, such as Adobe Illustrator files, is still in development. ## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who do not require extensive integrations with third-party apps
* Medium-sized teams (10-50 users) who prioritize data ownership and self-hosting capabilities
* Large enterprises (over 50 users) who require customization options and scalability
* Individuals who value open-source software and self-hosting
* Teams who do not require advanced features like video editing or 3D modeling

Yes, Penpot is free and open-source. However, self-hosting requires server costs.

Yes, Penpot is scalable and suitable for large teams, but it requires self-hosting and technical expertise.
### Does Penpot have a user-friendly interface?

comparison_markdown:
# Sketch vs Penpot

## Overview

Mac-only UI design tool popular with product designers. is a popular proprietary tool in the design space. Penpot is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Sketch costs $9-$20/user/month; Penpot is Free
- **License**: Sketch is Proprietary; Penpot is MPL 2.0
- **Data ownership**: Penpot can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Penpot eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Penpot has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Sketch | Penpot |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $9-$20/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$450/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,800/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Sketch

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Penpot

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [penpot/penpot](https://github.com/penpot/penpot) * ~33k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Sketch if:** Sketch is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Penpot if:** Penpot is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Sketch in its standard export format, review Penpot import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Penpot is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Sketch tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Penpot instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Sketch, switching to self-hosted Penpot will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Sketch until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Sketch paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Penpot free to use?
Yes. Penpot is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Sketch to Penpot?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Sketch data, follow the Penpot import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Penpot get regular updates?
Yes. Penpot has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Penpot without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Penpot development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Sketch](https://sketch.com) and [Penpot](https://penpot.app) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Penpot is a free, self-hosted alternative to Sketch. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.
